title: Boundary and seeded random CUDA fixtures against the CPU path, with allocator-level out-of-bounds checking

named.minimum_grid: 11 x 11 x 11 cells with 3 CPML cells per face, the smallest grid Region admits (five interior cells); Ez point source and monitor at the centre, x-normal plane at x = 0
named.odd_sizes: 13 x 15 x 17 cells, x_min CPML 5 layers kappa 2.5, z_max 4 layers kappa 1.5, index-1.5 sphere, Hy source
named.index_boundaries: 14 x 13 x 12 cells; an index-2 box whose +x face lies one cell beyond the PML interface and whose -y face lies on it; Ex source on the last interior cell of x and z; Ex monitor on the last interior cells of x, y and z corners; x-normal plane at the last interior x cell spanning the interior
named.strong_contrast: 15 x 13 x 13 cells, 4 CPML cells, epsilon 16 sphere (index 4) in epsilon 1, PEC wall on x_max (the solver has no PEC volume material; PEC is a boundary face)
named.ade_odd: 15 x 13 x 17 cells, Lorentz box (ADE P/Q states), y_min CPML 5 layers kappa 2, z_max 4 layers

random.draws: PML depth 3-5; one extra face with 3-5 layers and kappa in [1, 3]; a PEC face with probability 0.35; cells per axis from 2*pml+5 to 2*pml+11 (odd and even); steps 20-40; Lorentz material with probability 0.3 else epsilon uniform in [1, 16]; box or sphere with a face on or one cell beyond the PML interface with probability 0.4; source component among Ex..Hz; source on the last interior cell of one axis with probability 0.4; random monitor; x-normal plane spanning the interior (one cell short of a PEC wall)
random.precision: float64 so that any indexing defect is visible at the float64 tolerance

streamed.meaning: slab_width 5 on 13 cells leaves a 3-cell remainder slab; temporal_depth 3 on 20 steps leaves a 2-step remainder; slab 4 with depth 7 leaves a 1-cell slab and a 6-step remainder with three asynchronous tile buffers

cuda_paths: cuda_kernel fused + cuda_monitor_kernel fused, CUDA graph

out_of_bounds_check.method: the whole file run with PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1 (every tensor is a fresh cudaMalloc, so an out-of-bounds access has no cached neighbour to land in) and CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 (a faulting launch is reported at that launch, not later); CUDA graphs cannot be captured under a non-caching allocator, so this run launches the fused kernels and monitors eagerly while the ordinary run captures them in a graph
out_of_bounds_check.compute_sanitizer: not usable on this host: the installed compute-sanitizer is CUDA 11.6 and reports 'Target application terminated before first instrumented API call' against the CUDA 12.6 runtime torch 2.10.0+cu126 uses
out_of_bounds_check.race_check: the fused path is run twice per fixture and must be bitwise identical; this detects nondeterministic races only, not benign ones

reference_method: Simulation with backend='cpu' (numpy Yee/CPML/ADE backend of the fdtd grid package) at the fixture precision for the named and random fixtures; DifferentiableSimulation on CPU (torch) for the streamed fixture; a layer-A discrete comparison, not an independent physics oracle

observables.name: signals
observables.definition: point monitor trace divided by max |signal_ref|

observables.name: plane
observables.definition: x-normal plane DFT fields divided by max |field_ref|

observables.name: streamed signals and gradient
observables.definition: StreamedSimulation signals and epsilon gradient divided by the resident CPU maxima

observables.name: determinism
observables.definition: two fused graph runs are bitwise identical

acceptance.determinism: bitwise identity of the repeated fused run
acceptance.out_of_bounds: the file passes under PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1 and CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 with no CUDA error

not_yet_covered: compute-sanitizer memcheck and racecheck on a host with a CUDA 12.x toolkit: not available here
the same fixtures on a second CUDA platform (RTX 5880 Ada): prepared, not run here

notes: Every grid is at most 21 cells per axis. The CPU reference for the named and random fixtures is the numpy backend, the same discretization the torch path evaluates; the streamed fixture's reference is the torch CPU resident path.
